**Client:** Tarkington Business Futures Institute (TBFI), Cal Poly Pomona\
**Project:** Simulated Market Research at Scale: An AI Consultant-Training Simulation and Emerging-Industry Insights Dashboard\
**Project alignment:** PO3 : TBFI promotion and business intake\
**Proposed journey:** Website visit → demo engagement → business inquiry → qualification review→ sponsor meeting

# Analytics Blueprint

## Purpose

This report develops a digital measurement plan for TBFI’s project, *Simulated Market Research at Scale: An AI Consultant-Training Simulation and Emerging-Industry Insights Dashboard*. The plan focuses on how prospective sponsors, including small and medium-sized businesses in the San Gabriel Valley, discover these offerings, engage with the demo, and submit business inquiries.

The primary outcome is **qualified business inquiries (QBI)**, with sponsor meetings as a supporting outcome. GA4 will help measure website engagement and inquiry submissions, while TBFI will assess inquiry quality using consistent criteria and maintain records of qualification and meetings. This is a proposed plan for future implementation; evaluating AI research validity and consultant learning outcomes remains part of the broader capstone.

## Measurement Questions and KPIs

The following questions guide how TBFI will measure its digital outreach and business-intake process. Each question is linked to a KPI, a measurement definition, and a proposed data source. GA4 will track website activity, while TBFI’s inquiry records will confirm qualification and sponsor meetings. Results should use a consistent reporting period.

| Measurement question | KPI | How it is measured | Data source |
|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|
| Which channels bring visitors who engage with TBFI’s website? | Sessions and engagement rate | Compare visits and the percentage of engaged sessions across channels. | GA4 |
| Does the landing page encourage visitors to try the demo? | Demo start rate | Percentage of sessions on eligible landing pages that include a demo start. | GA4 |
| Do visitors complete the demo, and where do they stop? | Demo completion rate and step drop-off | Percentage of started demo attempts that are completed; identify steps where visitors stop. | GA4 |
| Does demo engagement lead to business inquiries? | Demo-to-inquiry rate | Percentage of completed demo attempts linked to a successful inquiry submission, where tracking allows. | GA4 and inquiry records |
| Which channels generate qualified inquiries and sponsor meetings? | Qualified business inquiries (QBI) and meetings booked | Count unique inquiries meeting TBFI’s qualification criteria and qualified inquiries resulting in a confirmed meeting, by channel where available. | TBFI inquiry and meeting records |

### Measurement Guidelines

-   A **valid inquiry** is a unique, non-test submission that TBFI can review. Spam and duplicate submissions should be excluded.
-   A **qualified inquiry** is a valid inquiry that meets criteria approved by TBFI, such as a relevant organizational need and a reasonable fit with TBFI's services.
-   A **confirmed meeting** is a scheduled meeting recorded by TBFI. Rescheduled meetings should not be counted as new inquiries.
-   Report direct inquiries separately from inquiries that followed demo use. A prospect may contact TBFI without using the demo.
-   Use GA4 to understand website behavior. Use TBFI's lead records to report qualification and meeting outcomes. If those records are not available, label the related KPIs “not available” rather than treating them as zero.
-   Do not send names, email addresses, phone numbers, or inquiry text to GA4. Use only the information needed for aggregate analysis and follow TBFI's consent and privacy requirements.
-   The channel attribution approach and reporting period should be documented before comparing lead quality across campaigns.

# **KPI Framework**

The proposed framework shows how website visits, demo engagement, and inquiry submissions connect to qualified business inquiries and sponsor meetings. Each metric measures a different stage and should be evaluated separately.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  QBI["Qualified business inquiries"]
  Traffic["Website visits"]
  Demo["Demo engagement"]
  Inquiry["Inquiry submissions"]
  Outcome["Qualified inquiries and meetings"]
  QBI --> Traffic
  QBI --> Demo
  QBI --> Inquiry
  QBI --> Outcome
  Traffic --> Sessions["Sessions by channel"]
  Demo --> Start["Demo starts"]
  Demo --> Complete["Demo completions"]
  Inquiry --> Forms["Form starts and submissions"]
  Outcome --> Rate["Qualification and meeting rates"]
```

Will be comparing results by channel, campaign, landing page, device, and demo version to identify where visitors drop off and which outreach efforts generate qualified business inquiries.

# Event Map

The event map outlines the visitor actions TBFI plans to track. It uses existing GA4 events where appropriate and proposed custom events for demo activity. Final tracking will depend on the website, demo, and inquiry form setup.

| Action | Event name | When it fires | Key details |
|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|
| View a page | `page_view` | A visitor opens a website page. | Page URL and page title. |
| Click the demo button | `select_content` | A visitor clicks “Start Demo.” | Button location; `content_type = demo_cta`. |
| Start the demo | `demo_start` — custom | The first interactive demo step loads after the visitor chooses to begin. | Demo attempt ID, version, and mode (intake or training). |
| Complete a demo step | `demo_step_complete` — custom | A visitor successfully completes a required step. | Demo attempt ID, step, version, and mode. |
| Complete the demo | `demo_complete` — custom | A visitor finishes all required demo steps. | Demo attempt ID, version, and mode; count once per completed attempt. |
| Start an inquiry form | `form_start` | A visitor first interacts with the inquiry form. | Form identifier; check existing tracking to avoid duplicates. |
| Submit an inquiry | `generate_lead` | The system confirms a successful inquiry submission. | Form identifier and anonymous inquiry ID; count once per submission. |
| Book a sponsor meeting | `meeting_booked` — optional custom | The booking system confirms a meeting. | Anonymous inquiry and booking IDs, if integration is available. |

# Validation Checklist and Test Cases

Proposed checks should be completed before TBFI relies on the results.

## Pre-launch Checklist

-   [ ] Confirm that page views and campaign links appear correctly in GA4.
-   [ ] Click each tracked demo button and verify that it records once.
-   [ ] Start and complete the demo; confirm events appear in the correct order.
-   [ ] Submit a valid test inquiry and confirm it is counted once.
-   [ ] Test a form with missing required information; it should not count as a successful inquiry.
-   [ ] Check that no names, contact details, or free-text responses are sent to GA4.
-   [ ] Test the website on desktop and mobile.
-   [ ] Verify tracking follows the approved consent settings.
-   [ ] Compare test submissions with TBFI’s inquiry records and document tracking gaps.

## Sample Test Cases

| Test | Steps | Expected result |
|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|
| Website visit | Open a tagged campaign link and visit the landing page. | GA4 records the page view and expected campaign information. |
| Demo use | Click the demo button, start the demo, and complete its required steps. | Click, start, step, and completion events appear in order without duplicates. |
| Inquiry submission | Submit a valid test inquiry, then refresh the confirmation page. | One successful inquiry is recorded and matches TBFI’s inquiry records. Refreshing does not create a duplicate. |
| Form error | Submit the form with required information missing. | No successful inquiry event is recorded. |
| Privacy and consent | Test with analytics consent accepted and declined; inspect the event data. | Tracking follows the approved consent settings and excludes personal information. |

::: {.callout-note title="Recording Test Results Notes"}
Record the test date, tester, result (pass, fail, or pending), and any issue requiring follow-up. Mark a test as passed only when its expected result is verified. If a feature or integration is unavailable, mark the test as pending.
:::
